question: A person borrowed some money on simple interest. After 4 years, he returned (9)/(5) of the money to lender. What was the rate of interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Principal be 5 units.

Amount returned = 9 units ⇒ Total Interest = 9 − 5 = 4 units.

Interest for 4 years = 4 units ⇒ Interest for 1 year = 1 unit.

Rate of Interest = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100.

Rate = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20% p.a.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount (A) = 9/5 of Principal (P)

Time (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount = P + SI

 
 Principal = 5 units
 
 
 Interest = 4 units

 

 Total Amount Returned = 9 units

 Time (T) = 4 Years

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Principal (P) = x

⇒ Amount (A) = 9x/5

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) = A − P = 9x/5 − x = 4x/5

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 4x/5 = (x × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 4/5 = 4R ÷ 100

⇒ 4/5 = R ÷ 25

⇒ R = (4 × 25) ÷ 5

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 5 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is calculated uniformly on the original principal throughout the loan period. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Formula

The total money paid back to the lender is called the Amount. Formula: Amount = Principal + Simple Interest.

Effective Rate of Interest

In Simple Interest, the effective rate for 'T' years is simply (R × T)%. For example, 20% p.a. for 4 years means the total interest generated is 80% of the Principal.
